content:
I'm happy to annouce the first release of Lean4Less, a tool for translating Lean to smaller theories by eliminating certain definitional equalities through the use of axioms. It's currently capable of eliminating both proof irrelevance and K-like reduction from Lean via the introduction of a single proof irrelevance axiom:

axiom prfIrrel {P : Prop} (p q : P) : p = q

translating it to a theory that I call "Lean-".

The implementation is based on @Mario Carneiro 's Lean4Lean, an implementation of the Lean kernel in Lean. I'm currently writing a paper on it that should be done in the next few weeks, but for now you can see the README and these slides for more details.

It unfortunately doesn't currently scale up to Mathlib as a whole, and also might abort the translation of certain constants due to the particularities of the current definition of Nat.gcd (see the "Caveats/Limitations" section of the README), but you may get lucky if you attempt to translate some lower-level Mathlib modules. (and of course, please let me know if you encounter any errors while translating)

I've implemented this as part of my PhD project for helping me translate Lean to Dedukti (and eventually to other proof assistants), so eventual Lean proof export is a major goal here. The translation framework should also be consistent with a general extensional-to-intensional translation, so it could be possible to extend it and integrate it with the elaborator or as a tactic to enable some kind of limited extensional-like reasoning in Lean -- in fact, I plan to discuss/try implementing something in this direction with @Sebastian Ullrich and others next month.
